summary: Rec Room was a social virtual world platform with an in-headset building tool and a Unity-based external editor called Rec Room Studio. It closed permanently on 1 June 2026 and its website went offline; its own shutdown notice told creators they could not download a working copy of their rooms, so every world built in it is now both unreachable and unrecoverable. What Rec Room did publish to creators covered its visual scripting language, a container-based scene hierarchy, a per-object authority model and a hard object budget, while the format of a room, the wire protocol, the avatar bone list and the transport for voice were never published at all. The traffic ran one way: the editor ingested assets authored in Unity, Blender and Maya, and nothing runnable ever came back out. The trap for a standards reader is where the documentation lived: Rec Room's own creator site said the editor's documentation was in a private chat server, and the site's documentation hub linked mostly to community-written pages that it explicitly disclaimed. Rec Room is the clearest worked example in this map of what a closed platform costs when its operator stops: the addresses, the inventory, the accounts and the content all ceased to exist on one day.

coverage.note: The client drew scenes to pixels itself and creators were told to tune draw calls, static batching and occlusion culling in the Unity-based editor, but the pass structure of the runtime renderer was never published, so this is visible only through performance advice.

coverage.note: Read only, and never with a format of its own: the editor took models authored in Unity, Blender and Maya into Rec Room, and Rec Room's own asset packs arrived as Unity package files, but no file ever carried a Rec Room room back out. At shutdown, on 2026-04-06, the operator added an export of the underlying room and invention data for rebuilding elsewhere, Steam PC only, while stating that a working copy of a room could not be downloaded. So the outbound direction holds raw data for reconstruction, not a room another runtime can open.

coverage.note: Rooms were named and reached only through the operator's own website and client, with no second resolver and no fallback.
